candidate.answerReason: Combining equal bases adds the exponents to 13, and combining equal exponents gives (4·9)^13.

methods.label: Combine equal bases and equal exponents
methods.explanation:
Group the factors with the same base. Multiplying powers with the same base adds their exponents, so
\[
4^4\cdot9^4\cdot4^9\cdot9^9
=4^{4+9}\cdot9^{4+9}
=4^{13}\cdot9^{13}.
\]
The two remaining powers have the same exponent. Using \(a^n b^n=(ab)^n\), the product becomes
\[
(4\cdot9)^{13}=\boxed{36^{13}},
\]
choice \(\text{C}\).
methods.levelReason: Only positive integer exponent laws and regrouping products are required.
